Task 1: Import Libraries¶

This section imports all required libraries for data handling, visualisation, neural network construction, evaluation and plotting.

In [1]:
# ============================================================
# MNIST Image Classification using MLP and CNN
# ============================================================

# -----------------------------
# 1. Import required libraries
# -----------------------------
import os
import time
import random
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers, callbacks

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, classification_report, ConfusionMatrixDisplay

# Reproducibility
SEED = 42
random.seed(SEED)
np.random.seed(SEED)
tf.random.set_seed(SEED)

print("TensorFlow version:", tf.__version__)

TensorFlow version: 2.20.0

Task 2: Import and Preprocess Dataset¶

Task 2a: Load and preprocess MNIST Dataset¶

In [2]:
# -----------------------------
# 2. Load and preprocess MNIST
# -----------------------------
(x_train_full, y_train_full), (x_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()

print("Original training shape:", x_train_full.shape)
print("Original test shape:", x_test.shape)

# Scale pixel values from 0–255 to 0–1
x_train_full = x_train_full.astype("float32") / 255.0
x_test = x_test.astype("float32") / 255.0

# Fixed validation split for fair model comparison
x_train_img, x_val_img, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    x_train_full,
    y_train_full,
    test_size=0.10,
    random_state=SEED,
    stratify=y_train_full
)

# Flattened data for MLP
x_train_mlp = x_train_img.reshape(-1, 28 * 28)
x_val_mlp = x_val_img.reshape(-1, 28 * 28)
x_test_mlp = x_test.reshape(-1, 28 * 28)

# 4D image data for CNN
x_train_cnn = x_train_img.reshape(-1, 28, 28, 1)
x_val_cnn = x_val_img.reshape(-1, 28, 28, 1)
x_test_cnn = x_test.reshape(-1, 28, 28, 1)

print("MLP training shape:", x_train_mlp.shape)
print("CNN training shape:", x_train_cnn.shape)

Task 3: Build Classifier using MLP¶

Task 3.0: Make some helper functions.¶

In [4]:
# -----------------------------
# 4. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

def get_callbacks(model_name):
    """
    Early stopping prevents unnecessary training after validation performance stops improving.
    ModelCheckpoint saves the best model separately for each architecture.
    """
    return [
        callbacks.EarlyStopping(
            monitor="val_loss",
            patience=3,
            restore_best_weights=True
        ),
        callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
            filepath=f"{model_name}_best.keras",
            monitor="val_loss",
            save_best_only=True
        )
    ]


def plot_training_curves(history, title):
    """
    Plot accuracy and loss curves separately.
    """
    # Accuracy curve
    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
    plt.plot(history.history["accuracy"], label="Training Accuracy")
    plt.plot(history.history["val_accuracy"], label="Validation Accuracy")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
    plt.title(f"{title}: Accuracy Curve")
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.show()

    # Loss curve
    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
    plt.plot(history.history["loss"], label="Training Loss")
    plt.plot(history.history["val_loss"], label="Validation Loss")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Loss")
    plt.title(f"{title}: Loss Curve")
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.show()


def evaluate_model(model, x_test_data, y_test_data, model_name):
    """
    Evaluate model using test loss, test accuracy, confusion matrix and classification report.
    """
    test_loss, test_acc = model.evaluate(x_test_data, y_test_data, verbose=0)

    y_prob = model.predict(x_test_data, verbose=0)
    y_pred = np.argmax(y_prob, axis=1)

    print(f"\n===== {model_name} Evaluation =====")
    print(f"Test Loss: {test_loss:.4f}")
    print(f"Test Accuracy: {test_acc:.4f}")

    print("\nClassification Report:")
    print(classification_report(y_test_data, y_pred, digits=4))

    cm = confusion_matrix(y_test_data, y_pred)
    disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix=cm)
    disp.plot(cmap="Blues", values_format="d")
    plt.title(f"{model_name}: Confusion Matrix")
    plt.show()

    return test_loss, test_acc, y_pred


def count_parameters(model):
    return model.count_params()

Task 3a: Build Baseline MLP Model¶

A Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model is constructed using fully connected dense layers with ReLU activation. Softmax activation is used in the output layer for multi-class classification.

In [5]:
# -----------------------------
# 5. Build MLP (Multilayer Perceptron) models
# -----------------------------

def build_mlp_model(optimizer="adam", dropout=False, deeper=False):
    model = keras.Sequential()

    model.add(layers.Input(shape=(784,)))

    if deeper:
        model.add(layers.Dense(256, activation="relu"))
        if dropout:
            model.add(layers.Dropout(0.30))

        model.add(layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"))
        if dropout:
            model.add(layers.Dropout(0.30))

        model.add(layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"))

    else:
        model.add(layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"))
        if dropout:
            model.add(layers.Dropout(0.20))

        model.add(layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"))
        if dropout:
            model.add(layers.Dropout(0.20))

    model.add(layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"))

    model.compile(
        optimizer=optimizer,
        loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )

    return model

Task 4 and 5: Compile and train/test model¶

Applied loss function defined above, used SGD, RMSPROP and ADAM optimizers, and calculate metrics¶

In [6]:
# -----------------------------
# 6. Optimizer comparison using same MLP architecture
# -----------------------------

# sgd: Stochastic Gradient Descent
# rmsprop: Room Mean Square Propagation
# adam: Adaptive Moment Estimation

optimizers = ["sgd", "rmsprop", "adam"]
optimizer_results = []
optimizer_histories = {}

for opt in optimizers:
    print(f"\nTraining MLP with {opt.upper()} optimizer...")

    model = build_mlp_model(optimizer=opt, dropout=False, deeper=False)

    start_time = time.time()

    history = model.fit(
        x_train_mlp,
        y_train,
        validation_data=(x_val_mlp, y_val),
        epochs=20,
        batch_size=32,
        callbacks=get_callbacks(f"mlp_{opt}"),
        verbose=1
    )

    training_time = time.time() - start_time

    test_loss, test_acc, _ = evaluate_model(
        model,
        x_test_mlp,
        y_test,
        f"MLP ({opt.upper()})"
    )

    best_val_acc = max(history.history["val_accuracy"])
    best_val_loss = min(history.history["val_loss"])
    final_train_acc = history.history["accuracy"][-1]
    final_val_acc = history.history["val_accuracy"][-1]

    optimizer_results.append({
        "Model": f"MLP ({opt.upper()})",
        "Optimizer": opt,
        "Parameters": count_parameters(model),
        "Best Validation Accuracy": best_val_acc,
        "Best Validation Loss": best_val_loss,
        "Test Accuracy": test_acc,
        "Test Loss": test_loss,
        "Overfitting Gap": final_train_acc - final_val_acc,
        "Training Time (sec)": training_time
    })

    optimizer_histories[opt] = history

    plot_training_curves(history, f"MLP ({opt.upper()})")

    verbose=1
)

dropout_time = time.time() - start_time

    mlp_dropout,
    x_test_mlp,
    y_test,
    "MLP with Dropout"
)

plot_training_curves(history_dropout, "MLP with Dropout")

CNN Extension Model¶

A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is additionally implemented to compare performance with MLP architectures. CNNs preserve spatial image structure and are widely used for image classification tasks.

In [9]:
# -----------------------------
# 9. CNN (Convoluted Neural Network) extension model
# -----------------------------

def build_cnn_model():
    model = keras.Sequential([
        layers.Input(shape=(28, 28, 1)),

        layers.Conv2D(32, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation="relu"),
        layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2)),

        layers.Conv2D(64, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation="relu"),
        layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2)),

        layers.Flatten(),

        layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"),
        layers.Dropout(0.50),

        layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")
    ])

    model.compile(
        optimizer="adam",
        loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )

    return model


print("\nTraining CNN extension model...")

cnn_model = build_cnn_model()
cnn_model.summary()

start_time = time.time()

history_cnn = cnn_model.fit(
    x_train_cnn,
    y_train,
    validation_data=(x_val_cnn, y_val),
    epochs=20,
    batch_size=32,
    callbacks=get_callbacks("cnn_model"),
    verbose=1
)

cnn_time = time.time() - start_time

cnn_test_loss, cnn_test_acc, _ = evaluate_model(
    cnn_model,
    x_test_cnn,
    y_test,
    "CNN Extension"
)

plot_training_curves(history_cnn, "CNN Extension")

    {
        "Model": "MLP with Dropout",

        "Parameters": count_parameters(mlp_dropout),

        "Best Validation Loss": min(history_dropout.history["val_loss"]),
        "Test Accuracy": dropout_test_acc,
        "Test Loss": dropout_test_loss,
        "Overfitting Gap": history_dropout.history["accuracy"][-1] - history_dropout.history["val_accuracy"][-1],
        "Training Time (sec)": dropout_time
    },
    {
        "Model": "Deep MLP",
        "Optimizer": "adam",
        "Parameters": count_parameters(deep_mlp),
        "Best Validation Accuracy": max(history_deep.history["val_accuracy"]),
        "Best Validation Loss": min(history_deep.history["val_loss"]),
        "Test Accuracy": deep_test_acc,
        "Test Loss": deep_test_loss,
        "Overfitting Gap": history_deep.history["accuracy"][-1] - history_deep.history["val_accuracy"][-1],
        "Training Time (sec)": deep_time
    },
    {
        "Model": "CNN Extension",
        "Optimizer": "adam",
        "Parameters": count_parameters(cnn_model),
        "Best Validation Accuracy": max(history_cnn.history["val_accuracy"]),
        "Best Validation Loss": min(history_cnn.history["val_loss"]),
        "Test Accuracy": cnn_test_acc,
        "Test Loss": cnn_test_loss,
        "Overfitting Gap": history_cnn.history["accuracy"][-1] - history_cnn.history["val_accuracy"][-1],
        "Training Time (sec)": cnn_time
    }
])

final_results = pd.concat([all_results, extra_results], ignore_index=True)

final_results = final_results.sort_values(
    by="Test Accuracy",
    ascending=False
).reset_index(drop=True)

final_results
